concepts.def: Linear feeding sequence: sun, producer, consumer, predator.
Network of interconnected food chains in one ecosystem.
Movement of nutrients between biomass, litter and soil stores.
Carbon moves through air, plants, animals, soils and oceans.
Latitude, altitude and ocean currents fix each biome's climate.
Variety of species in a place; high in tropical rainforests. 🦜

walkthroughs.body_html:
A food chain shows energy flow.

Only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.

So top predators are rare.

Nutrients move in a cycle.

Three stores: biomass, litter and soil.

In rainforests, biomass dominates; in tundra, litter does.

Climate decides biome.

Latitude controls sunlight; altitude controls temperature.

Ocean currents shift rainfall: e.g. the Atacama is dry because of cold currents.
